classification.difficultyReason: Select a similar pair from three differently oriented triangles, justify the test and match vertex order.

content.prompt:
For each set of three triangles, choose the two that are similar.
Choose the appropriate test and write a similarity statement (e.g. $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle FGH$).

spec.description: Three triangles in one comparison row, preserving vertex orientation and the two angle-label leaders on GHI.
spec.mathematics: ABC: A=50°, B=95°. DEF: D=50°, F=45°. GHI: H=95°, I=35°. No inferred angles appear in the question figure.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; supplied blue answers are held in the part answer.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GHI$ by AAA: at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$\angle C=180^\circ-50^\circ-95^\circ=35^\circ$.
$\angle G=180^\circ-95^\circ-35^\circ=50^\circ$.
Thus $\angle A=\angle G=50^\circ$ and $\angle B=\angle H=95^\circ$.
$\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GHI$ by AAA, since at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.

spec.description: Three right triangles in one comparison row with all six measurements and right-angle squares.
spec.mathematics: ABC: right angle A, AC=6, CB=10. DEF: right angle D, FD=2, FE=5. GHI: right angle G, IG=12, IH=20.
spec.answerVisibility: Unlabelled sides remain unlabelled. No calculated lengths or supplied answer appear.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GHI$ by RHS: both are right-angled, and their hypotenuses and one pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
answer.worked:
$\angle A=\angle G=90^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{BC}{HI}&=\frac{10}{20}=\frac12\\\frac{AC}{GI}&=\frac{6}{12}=\frac12\end{aligned}$$
The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GHI$ by RHS.

spec.description: Three differently oriented triangles in one row. Included-angle leaders are retained at B and G.
spec.mathematics: ABC: BC=2, BA=1.5, B=130°. DEF: DE=1.2, DF=1.8, D=130°. GHI: GH=0.6, GI=0.9, G=130°. Geometry is generated from the included angles and adjacent side ratios.
spec.answerVisibility: All six given lengths and three included angles are visible; proportionality calculations and the selected pair are answer-only.

answer.short: $\triangle DEF\sim\triangle GHI$ by SAS: two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$\angle D=\angle G=130^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{DE}{GH}&=\frac{1.2}{0.6}=2\\\frac{DF}{GI}&=\frac{1.8}{0.9}=2\end{aligned}$$
Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles are equal.
Therefore $\triangle DEF\sim\triangle GHI$ by SAS.

spec.description: Three isosceles triangles in one row: ABC upright, DEF pointing right and GHI pointing left. Double, single and triple equal-side ticks distinguish the three figures.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC=10, BC=5; DF=DE=2.62, FE=1.32; GH=GI=6.5, HI=3.25. Only the six printed measurements are labelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Equal-side ticks are permanent givens. Deduced equal lengths and the similarity statement appear only in answers.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GHI$ by SSS: all three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
answer.worked:
The equal-side marks give $AB=AC=10$ and $GH=GI=6.5$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{AB}{GH}&=\frac{10}{6.5}=\frac{20}{13}\\\frac{AC}{GI}&=\frac{10}{6.5}=\frac{20}{13}\\\frac{BC}{HI}&=\frac{5}{3.25}=\frac{20}{13}\end{aligned}$$
All three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GHI$ by SSS.
